explanations.answer: To the entrance to the Tent of Meeting
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The sisters walk right up to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation (Numbers 27:2). They didn't send a note or whisper to a cousin. They showed up in person, and I respect that a whole lot.

explanations.answer: To the banks of the Jordan
explanations.explanation: The Jordan is a river, and it's a good guess, but the sisters never go there in this passage. They go to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 27:2). That's where Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation are standing. If you tried to make your case by a river, friend, you'd mostly be talking to the water.

Manasseh is their own clan, so I see why you picked it. But the text sends them somewhere else: the entrance to the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 27:2). They stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation there. Talking to their own relatives would have been the easy road, and these five didn't take it.

Careful, friend, this one is a trap. The sisters say the opposite. Their father "was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD" (Numbers 27:3). They set that record straight before anybody could whisper it.

That's right, friend. The sisters say their father "was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD" (Numbers 27:3). Korah's rebellion was a big, loud mess (Numbers 16:1-3), and they made sure their dad's name stayed out of it. Then they said he died because of his own sin, and they didn't dodge that either.

Exactly. They say, "Give us property among our father's brothers" (Numbers 27:4). Their dad had no sons, and they didn't want his name to disappear from his clan. Five sisters, one clear request, no rambling. I've seen grown folks take twenty minutes to ask for a napkin.

explanations.answer: A seat among their clan's leaders
explanations.explanation: A seat sounds fancy, but that's not what they ask for. They say, "Give us property among our father's brothers" (Numbers 27:4). The request is about land and their father's name, not a title. I think they came with a plan, and the plan had a very short list.

Nope, no matchmaking in this passage. The sisters ask, "Give us property among our father's brothers" (Numbers 27:4). Husbands never come up in their request. They walked in with one item on the list, and it was property.

explanations.answer: He brings it before the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. "Moses brought their case before the LORD" (Numbers 27:5). He didn't guess and he didn't vote. When a question is that big, taking it straight to the LORD is the move.

explanations.answer: He hands it to the leaders
explanations.explanation: The leaders are standing right there, so I get it. But the text says Moses "brought their case before the LORD" (Numbers 27:5). He doesn't pass it down the line. Moses takes it to the One who actually has the answer.

Eleazar, the priest, is standing there too, so that's a fair guess. But the text never mentions lots here. It says Moses "brought their case before the LORD" (Numbers 27:5). No coin flip needed when you can ask the LORD Himself.

That's right. The LORD says, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly" (Numbers 27:7). Five sisters stood up in front of everybody, and the LORD agreed with them. I think that's the kind of sentence you'd frame and hang over the oven.
The LORD says the opposite. His words are, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly" (Numbers 27:7). The sisters weren't sent away and they weren't corrected. They were told they had it right.

Yes, friend. The LORD says to give them property "and transfer their father's inheritance to them" (Numbers 27:7). That's exactly what the sisters came for. Their father's name and his share stay in the family.

Debts, ha! I've had a few of those come my way, but they're not in this verse. The LORD says to transfer their father's inheritance to them (Numbers 27:7). That's the gift the sisters asked for, not a bill.

Duties are a good-sounding word, but the verse says something else. The LORD tells Moses to "transfer their father's inheritance to them" (Numbers 27:7). It's property they get, a share in the land. Nobody handed these five a to-do list.

That's it. "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter" (Numbers 27:8). That's the answer the five sisters walked in asking for. Now it's a rule for all Israel.

I see why you'd think of her, but the LORD names someone else. "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter" (Numbers 27:8). The widow isn't named in this rule. It's the daughter who comes next after sons.

The clan's leader doesn't show up in this rule at all. The LORD says, "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter" (Numbers 27:8). The inheritance stays with the man's own household first. That's good news for five sisters in particular.
Right on. "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers" (Numbers 27:9). The LORD takes it one step at a time, like a very organized recipe. Son first, then daughter, then brothers.

Servants aren't in the list, friend. The LORD says, "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers" (Numbers 27:9). The inheritance stays in the family line. It doesn't wander off to the household help.

Nice neighbors are a blessing, but they're not in this rule. The LORD says, "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers" (Numbers 27:9). The line keeps going through the man's own family first. Nobody's getting a surprise inheritance because they lived next door.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says to give it "to the next of kin from his clan" (Numbers 27:11). It stays in the clan, not with another tribe. That's the last step in the whole line.

Correct. When there are no children, no brothers, and no uncles on the father's side, the LORD says, "give his inheritance to the next of kin from his clan" (Numbers 27:11). It stays in the clan. The LORD built this rule so the family line keeps going all the way down.
